sections.html:
In Butler, three county desks field nearly every property tax call, all on West Dakota Street. The Collector/Treasurer is in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, MO 64730. Room 4 holds the Assessor and Room 1 the County Clerk. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, with a lunch closure from noon until 1 pm.

Reach the Collector at 660-679-3341 or through the courthouse line at 660-386-7776, option 3. The Assessor answers at option 4 on the courthouse line. Deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds in Room 3. Because the Collector doubles as county Treasurer, the same office takes in your payment and then sends the shares to schools, townships and the health center.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Bates County
sections.html:
Rural Bates County lies in west central Missouri near the Kansas line, within reach of Kansas City. Butler is the seat and biggest town. Population was 16,042 in 2020 and is estimated at 16,512 for 2025. Of 7,189 housing units, 11.1% stood empty, and owners lived in 74.3% of the occupied ones.

Your parcel falls in one of several school districts, among them Butler R-V, Adrian R-III, Rich Hill R-IV and Drexel R-IV, and the district drives some of the levy lines on your statement. Check the bill itself to see which applies.

sections.h2: When a Bates County tax bill turns delinquent
sections.html:
The cutoff is New Year's Day. RSMo 139.100 requires the collector to tack a penalty onto anything still open after January 1. A stamped envelope is credited on its postmark date, while registered or certified mail is credited on the day it was certified. If a postmark is smudged or missing, the collector decides and records the reason.

For 2026 bills, that makes December 31, 2026 the practical cutoff, with the new penalty arriving on January 1, 2027. A drop box on the east face of the Administration Building never closes.

Bates County Collector payment rules

There are four ways to settle a bill. Any card fee is charged to the payer, and Bates County keeps none of it, under RSMo 139.055.

  • In person at Room 2, 103 West Dakota, Butler.
  • By mail, stamped on or before the deadline.
  • On the Collector's website: $4.00 per debit payment, 2.45% on credit.
  • In the round-the-clock drop box beside the Administration Building's east wall.

If a license office asks for proof of payment, a receipt on your phone screen is enough.

sections.h2: How the Bates County tax sale works
sections.html:
Each August, on the fourth Monday, the Collector auctions certificates on delinquent real estate. Parcels on the list are published in July. To take one off, the full balance must be in the Collector's hands by 4:30 PM on the Friday before. Call the Collector for each year's exact dates and for how earlier sales turned out.

For a parcel already headed to sale, bring cash, a money order, a card or a cashier's check. The website and phone line won't take those payments.

Losing a parcel at auction isn't instant. RSMo 140.405 lets the owner buy it back, and the winning bidder has to mail a redemption notice, first class and certified, a full ninety days ahead of claiming any deed. Selling or borrowing against the land requires redeeming first, so get the redemption figure from the Collector before you list.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Bates County assessment
sections.html:
Begin in Room 4 and ask the Assessor to recheck your value. If that fails, go to the local Board of Equalization; the Clerk in Room 1 can tell you the meeting dates and book you in.

Beyond the board lies the State Tax Commission (RSMo 138.430). File by September 30 of the assessment year, or thirty days after the board's ruling if that is later, and upload the board's decision letter with the complaint.

An individual owner may represent themselves there. An LLC, trust, association or estate needs an attorney. The Commission's phone number is 573-751-1715.

Think the bill is wrong but don't want it to go delinquent? RSMo 139.031 lets you pay in full and object. Hand the Collector a written statement with your reasons and your claimed value. The part nobody disputes goes to the taxing districts, and the contested part is held apart.

Ninety days after filing, you must have sued the Collector in circuit court, unless an assessment appeal filed on time is already working through the Commission or a court, which then takes the suit's place.

A refund of tax paid by mistake requires a written application within three years.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or due
sections.html:
Before the contract date, get a payoff number from the Collector and ask whether older years show a balance. Hand the figure to the title company.

  • Tally every current and past-due real estate bill on the parcel.
  • Learn whether the parcel is on a sale list.
  • Ask the Assessor if a value change is pending.
  • Check that Room 3 will record the deed and any release of an old deed of trust.

Unpaid tax stays with the land, which is why title companies order a tax search early. A cash buyer wants the same search. With no lender involved, payoff and recording can wrap up in one visit once the Collector confirms a zero balance, and nobody waits on an underwriter.

sections.h2: Timeline for a Bates County sale
sections.html:
A tax-clean sale takes only a few calls, and it helps to make them in order.

  1. Call 660-679-3341 and ask the Collector for the balance on the parcel, including any earlier year.
  2. If the value looks off, visit Room 4 before you list and ask the Assessor to explain it.
  3. Send the payoff figure to the title company so it can prorate the current year at closing.
  4. Keep a copy of the paid receipt for each year you owned the property.
  5. After closing, the Recorder in Room 3 records the new deed, and the buyer's name goes on future statements.

Bills are mailed to the owner of record, so a seller who moves out should leave a forwarding address with the Collector. A missed statement doesn't excuse the tax or the penalty that starts after January 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property taxes in Bates County, Missouri?
faqs.a: Go to the Collector in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, or pay by mail, online or in the Administration Building drop box. The phone is 660-679-3341. Cards add a fee that you cover.

faqs.q: When does a Bates County property tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: Once December 31 ends. A penalty is added after January 1, and a mailed check counts on its postmark, so send it early enough to be stamped in time.

faqs.q: When is the Bates County tax sale?
faqs.a: Every year on the fourth Monday of August. To stop the auction, the full balance has to reach the office by 4:30 PM on the Friday before.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bates County property value?
faqs.a: Ask the Assessor in Room 4 first, then the Board of Equalization via the County Clerk. Beyond that is the Missouri State Tax Commission, with a filing date of September 30 or thirty days after the board's decision, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Can I pay my taxes under protest in Bates County?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay everything before the delinquency date and give the Collector your grounds in writing. Court action to recover the disputed amount must begin within ninety days unless an assessment appeal is already open.
